claim: Media Studio main has a bounded current-checkout Flatpak-builder/runtime smoke job using the required Flathub-compatible Freedesktop runtime branch, plus a protected manual VAAPI/NVENC self-hosted hardware matrix. This claim excludes production Flatpak sandbox readiness, host integration readiness, reproducible builds, and universal GPU availability.

output.claim_status: Supported by the supplied definitions within the stated boundary; live execution remains unverified.
output.summary: The CI file invokes the real Flatpak-builder action on push events, installs its bundle, and runs the packaged binary with bounded timeouts. The GPU workflow is manual, restricted to the upstream main ref, uses explicit self-hosted backend labels, and fail-closes on missing encoders, fallback, invalid output, or unverified results. Manifest parity and KIO permission contracts are present.
evidence_gaps: No external CI logs or self-hosted runner results were supplied.
CLI/profile wiring and log-path configuration are outside the bound files, so end-to-end consumer behavior is not independently evidenced.
supported_claims: Flatpak runtime branch 25.08 is used consistently in both manifests.
The GPU matrix contains VAAPI and NVENC entries with explicit runner labels and documented device requirements.
The hardware smoke checks exact encoders, disables software fallback, validates and decodes output, and requires hardware-use and RESULT=verified markers.
residual_risks: Mutable action references and networked dependency resolution remain; they must not be presented as reproducibility guarantees.
The broad Flatpak host permissions remain appropriate only for the explicitly experimental artifact.
Actual GPU availability and environment protection depend on external runner provisioning.
